notes.title: Civilization VII Update 1.2.2 – Jun 23
notes.content:
[p]Hey [i]Civ [/i]fans,[/p][p]
Update 1.2.2 is rolling out now![/p][p]We’ve been heads-down at Firaxis putting together a hefty update for you this June, packed with long-awaited features like Large and Huge Maps, expanded Advanced Game Options, and a community favorite: Steam Workshop support. This update also brings new Town Specializations, City-State Bonuses, Beliefs, balance changes, UI improvements, and yes – a very pettable Scout dog.[/p][p]For more context on what’s in this update, and what’s still being worked on beyond it, check out our recently released [u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/news/civ-vii-update-check-in-jun-10/"]Update Check-In[/url][/u].[/p][p]We’re also trying something new with this update. You’ll notice a (★) icon next to select notes: our way of showing that a feature or change was influenced by the community. If you don’t see this community icon next to something you’ve mentioned, know that it’s not a reflection on your feedback, it’s just a way to highlight some of the broader conversations we’re listening in on. Thanks for being part of the journey, and there’s more to come![/p][p]And lastly, a few quick notes before you dive in:[/p][list][*][p]While we aim to maintain backwards compatibility for existing saves as much as possible, some new abilities or effects may not appear until you start a new game or advance to the next Age in your current campaign. For the best experience, we recommend starting a new game, or continuing your current game into the next Age.[/p][/*][*][p]If you encounter any new bugs or issues, try disabling any mods, as some may not yet be compatible with the latest update.[/p][/*][*][p]Are you playing on Steam and want to finish your current save under a previous version? You can do so using our legacy Steam beta branch.[/p][/*][/list][p]Read on for the full notes below![/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcjtn8_p2zsIEeSxnPOecCCSCwZzW1_DiJpA0SEJxcjlGucstA4IJsLr7zVT_K5lc9eNwpiYiTOnq8lX7cQvyNFJIjxkm-lgwm3KG5PKtkBYcwKgB6oc0cdLjxD6q6dvFAwMw14Gg?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][h1][b]
Large and Huge Maps[/b][/h1][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf2kpX0gtHjtVu3awQrXPfiMxtHGeJqjXerRSSvQWk-LdJ5C6ZqDjDuKql_Zfm43pk6W0S7490pccLrI1CMIiedhZ1Ug5jVks9mHw7w42mgRmfmKHC2LuuGCRODi66-daSGNVYrYA?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][p]We wanted to take some time to get this feature right, and with 1.2.2, we’re happy to add support for Large and Huge map sizes on all of our map types – for when you really want to explore an epic world. 
[/p][p]Both map sizes default to 10 players, but multiplayer campaigns still max out at 8 total players, including AI and humans. Though 12 total players is still our goal for Huge maps, we need a bit more time to make sure increased player counts won’t compromise game stability or performance.
[/p][p]On maps this big, you’ll find yourself encountering new leaders and civs playing out their own local rivalries deep into the Exploration Age, and even the largest of empires will often find themselves struggling with other emerging superpowers in the Modern Age.
[/p][p]Because these maps are so large, we’ve added exciting new Pantheons, Religious Beliefs, Discoveries, and City-State bonuses to ensure there’s enough content for all the players in a game. More on those below. 
[/p][p]A quick heads-up that bigger maps have bigger hardware demands. On some systems, you might notice slower turn times or performance drops, especially on lower-end hardware. Lastly, Balanced starts on Large and Huge maps might encounter map generation oddities. We are actively working on improvements. On these map sizes, we recommend you stick to Standard starts instead of Balanced for the time being
 
[/p][h1][b]New Advanced Game Options[/b][/h1][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeGDPhcoj6xI7L7AwFBpjzC0KhXeyy_2flNRO7Ibmk3qeGMIUdbJ3leEkXCFLneqVkYyygZXz4vSEwq5qgRSd_mBN-95sMcQ6U0dweH-_gUh5HuDpajgQZ2i-e0UR-xIRIN2WzE?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][p]One of the best things about [i]Civilization [/i]is how many ways there are to play. Some players are happy to peacefully build the biggest, best Cities while others want to ignore all that and go conquer the world ("Yes, your amazing City [i]does [/i]look great in my empire"). With 1.2.2, we’ve added several new advanced game setup options to give you even more control over how you play. The below options are currently available only in singleplayer. 

The new options include:[/p][list][*][p]Enable or disable specific Legacy Paths per Age (or turn them all off entirely)[/p][/*][*][p]Disable Score Victory (unlimited turns in final Age)[/p][/*][*][p]Enable or disable specific Crises[/p][/*][*][p]Custom AI Difficulty Options (adjust each AI bonus independently)[/p][/*][*][p]Bypass Civ Unlocks on Age Transition (you’ll be able to pick ANY civ from the next Age during an Age transition, no matter what you’ve unlocked through your gameplay decisions)[/p][/*][*][p]Adjust Independent Power Hostility (all hostile, random, or all friendly)
[/p][/*][/list][p]We’ve had a lot of fun playing with different Legacy Paths on or off in each Age. While Legacy Paths that don’t lead to a Victory are always optional, sometimes it’s nice to just tune them out entirely and focus on playing into the unique strengths of your leader and civ. For a fun sandbox game we’ve been playing in the office, try turning off Legacy Paths for Antiquity and Exploration, and setting the game to Abbreviated Ages. If you want to lean into the sandbox feel even more, try turning off Legacy Paths in Modern and the Score Victory, too. 
[/p][p]This is a step toward giving you more flexibility in how you play, and we know Legacy Paths have more room to grow. Stay tuned for future updates![/p][p]
[/p][h1][b]New Bonuses for Religion, City-States, and Towns [/b][/h1][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXev3tjKQYwM3SkBpVPutv_XC_VajN9oArm2ysSh3UbsJOzx7hupmUo3et-Jffkzcx8CnP3Scbq_HhUpJT5sTWs6UPTdKFUPw2nVbwVchw1H8Y5WcKrJJDoZIhASJS0GhD1UxELYng?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][p]Pantheons are first come first serve, so to make sure there’s enough to go around, we’ve added two new Pantheons to Antiquity, and these can be selected by more than one player.
[/p][p]We’ve heard feedback from players that Religion in [i]Civ VII [/i]has room to grow. One consistent piece of feedback we’ve seen is that there’s not enough reason to convert your [b]own [/b]Settlements, so we’re adding new Beliefs and updating some existing ones that give bonuses for spreading your Religion within your own empire. We’ve got bigger and bolder changes on the horizon for Religion, too, so we’ll keep you updated on how it evolves![/p][p][/p][p]We’re also introducing updates for Town Focus bonuses to help them feel more impactful. Urban Centers in particular have received a glow-up, and now gain access to many of the Buildings that were otherwise only available in Cities (like Libraries and Monuments in Antiquity). Fort Towns gain the ability to purchase multiple walls so they can really lock down strategic chokepoints. We also introduced a new type of Town Focus: the Resort Town. These relaxing scenic retreats gain extra Gold and Happiness on Rural tiles with Happiness and increased Yields on Natural Wonders.[/p][p][/p][p]Lastly, we felt massed Hub Towns were overshadowing some of the other options and gave them a slight nerf from +2 Influence per connected Settlement to +1 Influence. We’re going to keep our eye on them to see how they compare against the other newly buffed Towns.

[/p][h1][b]Steam Workshop[/b][/h1][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdTP49_vhNgPGGZnW4OgGNePY_Vl6n_z4ouZofwR9wUfR8QGd-YcL-ZATQNHWP-1v6tsEkn9EOqtIt8M4ntG_8rakJXXfEEmt4ryNqLD6WJ2PVckIUJ-yJJIUv7x1ti413d8gkP?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We’ve added a lot of options to customize your experience with this update, but nothing beats the level of personalization you can achieve with the help of our amazing modding community. From UI tweaks to ambitious gameplay overhauls, mods provide a way to really make your gameplay experience unique. So with this update, we're also rolling out Steam Workshop support and an initial version of the Modding SDK.[/p][p][/p][p]You'll now be able to find and install mods from the Steam Workshop. Just hit the Subscribe button and your mods will be installed the next time you start up the game! For modders, this of course means your mods will be easier for players to find and download, and you'll be better able to keep the mod up-to-date for your users. Please note that the [i]Civilization VII[/i] mods you'll find in the Workshop are created by and for the [i]Civ[/i] community, and are not officially supported by Firaxis or 2K. Use them at your own risk![/p][p][/p][p]We’ll also be providing a Modding SDK to help our modding community create, debug, and upload mods to the Steam Workshop. While this initial version of the SDK won't feature art tools, it will include a mod uploader and the (glorious) return of FireTuner. Additionally, we've included some guides and documentation within the tools, if you’d like to learn how to make your own mods.
[/p][p]Last thing – we’ve also uploaded three example mods to the Steam Workshop to show off some of the things you can do with mods, but also as references for both new and more experienced modders on the various ways you can make changes to the game (there are a few neat tricks that weren’t available in [i]Civilization VI[/i])! [/p][p][/p][p]A quick reminder for modders:[/p][p]When you're creating and sharing mods, please make sure your content follows our User Rules (which you can find in Section 6 of our [u][url="https://www.take2games.com/eula/"]Terms of Service[/url][/u]), for example:[/p][list][*][p]Don’t use content based on someone else’s IP (like characters, music, or art from other games, movies, etc.) unless you have the rights to use it.[/p][/*][*][p]Keep content safe and respectful, meaning no harmful, offensive, or inappropriate material.[/p][/*][*][p]And of course, no malicious code or anything that could negatively impact the experience for other players.[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p][h1][b]New Loading Screen[/b][/h1][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXekuoCNqclykDM_jRJe-I2KqBm9mf9qpvVGKcTJtZh1CXYRQ1joajL5FyVKx0GKFYySgHB_I9ccQ0ZjLUgDyEV2qnTYqF1uhVVjsWJ8qPtDAWB8I_iPeI87jDgDmjuiXSApAFWC?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][p]Did someone say [b]more [/b]Gwendoline Christie VO? [/p][p][/p][p]One of the first things you’ll notice when you boot up 1.2.2 is a refreshed Loading Screen, a small but important step in a bigger effort to improve [i]Civilization VII’s [/i]UI. We’ve rethought how we develop the UI, and the Loading Screen gave us a great chance to try new workflows without disrupting gameplay. Highlights include leader portraits front and center, new info panels, a Tips & Hints section, and fully rewritten and rerecorded intros narrated by Gwendoline Christie. Want to dive deeper? Check out our [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/from-the-devs/"]latest article[/url] from Firaxis Lead Producer Tom Shaw on this change and what’s next for the UI.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcBXTziLLOzDOlp01A1Id4C7s2ELfE-H6tdVoUpf9eEZ2cNCqwDkHco-99qSD3ucJSpOTIYUdwEYc7LveWJ8zQ5I48HZLVu0liWsgsD3oPUohIXBs2GMMvKI17xDOi054k5iWGUDA?key=B0mRY1DaSC-3AGWZE1NIU9TT"][/img][/p][h1][b]Gameplay[/b][/h1][p][/p][h2]New Advanced Game Options[b] [/b][/h2][list][*][p](★) - Community Influenced Item] Added an option to pick and choose which Legacy Paths are enabled per Age.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note: [/b]We wanted to give players options for how they could customize their game by allowing them to turn off Legacy Paths of their choice, and allowing them to disable the Score Victory. Note that if you turn off all Legacy Paths, and disable the Score Victory, you can still win the game with a Domination Victory by eliminating all other leaders. We think this change should allow for a cool sandbox experience through the Ages! (Please note that currently these options are only available in Single-player, but we plan to add these to Multiplayer in the future.)[/p][list][*][p]Nuclear Fission Tech is added to the Modern Age, so players can still use nukes without completing the Military Legacy Path. [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p](★) Added an option to disable the Score Victory.[/p][/*][*][p](★) Added a new “Custom” AI Difficulty setting that allows the player to choose difficulty options specific for each value.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note[/b]: With this update, you can set any of the AI bonuses to any level you want individually. Don’t like the economic bonuses the AI has on Deity, but enjoy the challenge in combat? Now you can set up a game to do exactly that![/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p](★) Added an option to pick and choose which Crises you want on or off in your game.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note:[/b] We’ve always allowed for Crises to be entirely on or off, but wanted to give you the added control to pick and choose which Crises you want to see. If you have more than one Crisis enabled for an Age, then the game will randomly choose one from the pool of enabled Crises.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p](★) Added an option to Bypass Civilization Unlocks, allowing players to choose any civ for the next Age at Age Transition regardless of any unlock requirements.[/p][/*][*][p](★) Added an option to control initial Independent Power hostility. Settling within 5 tiles of an Independent Power will still cause them to become hostile.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note:[/b] Starting near multiple hostile IPs can make for a challenging early game, but sometimes you just want some space to build out your Capital.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Land-Based Treasure Convoys[/h2][list][*][p](★)  Treasure Fleets are growing legs! These will now be called Treasure Convoys, and you’ll be able to use them over land and not just the sea. Any Distant Lands Settlement with improved Treasure Resources now generates Treasure Convoys and no longer requires Coastal access, a Fishing Quay, or the Shipbuilding Tech.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note: [/b]The Treasure Fleet Legacy path, specifically the gameplay around gathering Resources not immediately available to your empire, is a fun collection minigame for players that like to play the map. While we’ve improved Resource placement further, the steps required to progress this Legacy Path were still quite restrictive and often forced linear play patterns instead of asking for interesting decisions when settling. We’ve made some adjustments that should make it much easier to pursue this Legacy Path, while still requiring you to explore and settle Distant Lands. We plan on continuing to observe this Legacy Path as well as the others to find places to inject strategic variety.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Shipbuilding is no longer required to make Treasure Convoys.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note[/b]: With this change, your Treasure Convoys will start their journey home while the Ocean is still dangerous, and your Units can still be damaged by stormy seas.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fishing Quays are no longer needed to make Treasure Convoys.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated tutorial and Advisor Quests to remove instances of Fishing Quay being required to spawn Treasure Convoy.
[/p][/*][/list][h2]AI[/h2][list][*][p]AI civs now repair damaged Buildings and Improvements over time in gameplay. [/p][/*][*][p]AI will now have better judgment and make smarter deals when negotiating a peace deal.[/p][/*][*][p]AI players will now activate a Great Person when they create one.[/p][/*][*][p]AI now prioritizes attacking Enemy Treasure Convoys when progressing through a game. [/p][/*][*][p]AI are no longer as aggressive in declaring war on players who are far away from them.[/p][/*][*][p]AI leaders can no longer build duplicate Buildings when one of their damaged Buildings has a hostile Unit on it.[/p][/*][*][p]AI civs will no longer build multiple Settler Units and not use them when encountered during late Antiquity gameplay.
[/p][/*][/list][h2]Cities & Towns[/h2][list][*][p]Added a brand new Town Focus,[b] Resort Town: [/b]+1/2/3 Happiness and +1/2/3 Gold on tiles with Happiness (Natural Appeal). +50% Yields on Natural Wonder tiles in this Town.[/p][/*][*][p]Redesigned [b]Urban Center[/b]: +100% Gold and Happiness towards Building maintenance in this Town. You can buy additional Buildings (e.g. Library, Bath, Monuments) in this Town (Was: +1 Science and Culture on Districts with two Buildings in this Town.)[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note:[/b] You can think of Urban Centers like a mini-City – useful for when you want some additional Buildings, but don't necessarily want another build queue to manage.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p](★) Adjusted balance on several existing Town Focuses: [/p][list][*][p][b]Religious site[/b]: +1 Happiness on all Buildings and +1 Relic Slot on Temples in this Town. (Was: +2 Happiness and +1 Relic Slot on Temples in this Town.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Factory Town[/b]: +100% Gold towards purchasing a Factory in this town. +1 Resource Slots. +5 Trade Range. (From +100% Gold towards purchasing a Factory in this Town. +1 Resource Slots.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mining Town[/b]: +2/3/4 Production on all Camps, Woodcutters, Clay Pits, Mines, and Quarries. (Was: +1/2/3 Production on all Camps, Woodcutters, Clay Pits, Mines, and Quarries.)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hub Town[/b]: +1 Influence for every connected Town (Was: +2 Influence for every connected Town.)[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note:[/b] The only nerf of the bunch, Hub Town has been tuned down slightly to bring it in line with other Towns. We’ll keep an eye on this Focus for further tweaks that may be needed.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Fort Town[/b]: +5 healing to Units and +25 health to Walls in this Town and can purchase additional Walls.
[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]Independent Powers & City-States[/h2][list][*][p](★) Added 24 new City-State bonuses across the Ages.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note[/b]: Bigger maps means more players, and more potential City-State allies. To support this, we added more options for Suzerain bonuses when befriending a City-State. One of these new options is also shareable, so multiple civs can choose it. We felt that having a good baseline option available to all players would be a good quality-of-life consideration. [/p][/*][*][p][b]New Antiquity City-State Bonuses: [/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Scientific[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Lingua Franca[/b]: +2 Science on displayed Codices.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Archimedes’ Screw[/b]: +1 Science on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dev Note[/b]: There are a few new bonuses that stack bonuses on Warehouse Buildings. This is part of an approach we're experimenting with to keep infrastructure Buildings like Warehouses relevant and impactful as more of your empire is swallowed up by urban sprawl.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Militaristic[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Hegemon[/b]: +1 Settlement Limit.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dev Note[/b]: Some players have asked for more ways to increase Settlement Limit. We’re pretty comfortable with the current limits and how they rein in overly-wide strategies, but this seemed like an appropriately-costed way to give those players an option.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Spoils of War[/b]: +1 War Support. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Economic[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Stockpiles[/b]: +2 Resource Capacity in the Capital.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ganzabara[/b]: +1 Gold on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Cultural[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Ennigaldi-Nanna’s Museum[/b]: +2 Culture on displayed Codices.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Papermaking[/b]: +1 Culture on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]New Exploration City-State Bonuses: [/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Scientific[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Master Tradesmen[/b]: +1 Science on Specialists.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Apprenticeship[/b]: +1 Science on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Militaristic[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Staked Claims[/b]: +1 Settlement Limit.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Casus Belli[/b]: +1 War Support. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Economic[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Bullion[/b]: +1 Gold on Treasure Resources.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Market Right[/b]: +1 Gold on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Cultural[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Sì Mín[/b]: +1 Culture on Specialists.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Artisans[/b]: +1 Culture on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]New Modern City-State Bonuses: [/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Scientific[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Refineries[/b]: +1 Science on slotted Factory Resources.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mechanization[/b]: +1 Science on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Militaristic[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Dependent Territories[/b]: +1 Settlement Limit.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Home Front[/b]: +1 War Support. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Economic[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Factory System[/b]: +1 Resource Capacity in Settlements with a Factory.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Entrepreneurship[/b]: +1 Gold on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Cultural[/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Touring Exhibits[/b]: +3 Culture on displayed Artifacts.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Textile Industry[/b]: +1 Culture on Warehouse Buildings. This bonus can be chosen by multiple civilizations.
[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]Economy[/h2][list][*][p]Made several balance adjustments to Specialists, especially in Modern. [/p][list][*][p][b]Free Speech[/b] (Modern Age Civic): +50% Food and Happiness towards maintaining Specialists (Was: +100% Food and Happiness towards maintaining Specialists)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Constitution[/b] (Exploration Age Civic): 25% Food and Happiness towards maintaining Specialists (Was: 50% Food and Happiness towards maintaining Specialists)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Attribute Node[/b]: 10% Food and Happiness towards maintaining Specialists, or +20% if you have 3 or fewer Cities (Was: 15% Food and Happiness towards maintaining Specialists, or +30% if you have 3 or fewer Cities)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Attribute Node[/b]: 15% of Food is refunded when a City grows by adding a Specialist. (Was: 25% of Food is refunded when a City grows by adding a Specialist.)[/p][/*][*][p][b][u]Fascism Ideology[/u][/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Assembly Line[/b]: +2 Production from Specialists. -2 Food in Towns. (Was:  +3 Production from Specialists. -3 Food in Towns)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dirigisme[/b]: +4 Gold from Specialists. -3 Happiness in Towns. (Was: +6 Gold from Specialists. -3 Happiness in Towns.)[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b][u]Communism Ideology[/u][/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Proletariat[/b]: +4 Food from Specialists. -3 Happiness in Towns (Was: +6 Food from Specialists. -3 Happiness in Towns.)[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Removed Gold Maintenance for Portal de Mercaderes, Steel Mill, and Manigramam. [/p][/*][*][p]Removed Happiness Maintenance for the Garden, Shiguan, Catedral, and Jardin à la Française.[/p][/*][*][p]The “Suffetes” Tradition now grants the bonus Yields to the specialized Towns when slotting the Policy.[/p][/*][*][p]Tiles in Settlements without a Baray now get pillaged/damaged during floods while playing as Khmer after studying Mousong.[/p][/*][*][p]Aerodrome and Rail Station can no longer be built on top of each other.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated ability and text for Terrace Farm, which now gives adjacent buildings Gold, instead of receiving gold for adjacent Buildings.[/p][/*][*][p]Multiple World Wonders can no longer be built on the same tile when moving the priority on the Production queue.[/p][/*][*][p]The Opera House now counts as a Diplomacy building.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now produce or purchase Buildings after the Jaguar Slayer has placed a Jaguar Trap on an Empty Urban District.[/p][/*][*][p]Salt and Truffles resources now apply 20% Production towards producing Units when slotted into a City.[/p][/*][*][p]Modifiers for City Park, Stock Exchange, Tenement, and Laboratory function correctly.
[/p][/*][/list][h2]Age Transition[/h2][list][*][p](★) All leader-recommended civs are now unlocked by default during Age transition. 
[/p][/*][/list][h2]Diplomacy[/h2][list][*][p]Reconciliation is now usable with multiple leaders at the same time.[/p][/*][*][p]Continental System's massive relationship penalty now functions similar to a Denounce sanction.[/p][/*][*][p]Hostile military no longer receives War Support combat bonus when using Kispoko Nena’to to attack with Shawnee Civic Telwatiki Mastery unlocked.
[/p][/*][/list][h2]Environment[/h2][list][*][p](★) All map types now guarantee enough traversable Ocean Tiles near the Poles.[/p][/*][*][p]The water/lake tiles in Homelands no longer appear as Distant Land when using Continents, Terra Incognita, and Pangaea Plus map types.[/p][/*][*][p]Sugar resource is now correctly considered a Bonus resource in Modern instead of an Empire resource.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue where Cocoa would disappear from the map when transitioning to Modern.

notes.title: Civilization VII's Steam Workshop is here!
notes.content:
[h1]Civilization VII's Steam Workshop is here![/h1][p][/p][p]As part of Update 1.2.2, Steam Workshop support is now live in [i]Civilization VII[/i]! With the [i]Civ VII [/i]Workshop, you can modify your journey through the Ages in [i]Civilization VII[/i] with user-made leaders, civs, maps, Narrative Events, and more, then share them with the [i]Civ [/i]community and rate your favorites to help boost their visibility![/p][p][/p][p]There's a massive amount of talent, passion, and creativity in the [i]Civ [/i]mod scene, so you're sure to find something exciting while browsing the [i]Civ VII [/i]Workshop. Once you've found a mod you'd like to try, hitting the "Subscribe" button on that mod's page will automatically download and enable the mod for use in [i]Civilization VII[/i]. You can enable or disable any downloaded mods by going to "Additional Content" in [i]Civilization VII[/i]'s main menu, then "Add-Ons" to turn any mods on or off! [/p][p][/p][p]To help [i]Civ VII [/i]mod makers get started, we're including some documentation in the tool, including a few best practices for mods. We’re also adding some simple example mods to the Workshop, made by a few of the folks on the dev team – including popular-modder-turned-Firaxis-developer Sukritact![/p][p][/p][p]We want to expand the functionality for [i]Civ VII [/i]modding in the future, with the goal of making it even easier to build your own creations and share them with the world. Please note that the [i]Civilization VII [/i]mods you'll find in the Workshop are created by and for the [i]Civ[/i] community, and are not officially supported by Firaxis or 2K. Use them at your own risk![/p][p][/p][h3][b]A quick reminder for modders:[/b][/h3][p]When you're creating and sharing mods, please make sure your content follows our User Rules (which you can find in Section 6 of our [url="https://www.take2games.com/eula/"][u]Terms of Service[/u][/url]), for example:[/p][list][*][p]Don’t use content based on someone else’s IP (like characters, music, or art from other games, movies, etc.) unless you have the rights to use it.[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Keep content safe and respectful, meaning no harmful, offensive, or inappropriate material.[/p][/*][*][p]And of course, no malicious code or anything that could negatively impact the experience for other players.
[/p][/*][/list][p]You can check out our full terms of service here. [/p][p][/p][p]We're so excited to be adding the much-requested Steam Workshop to [i]Civilization VII[/i], and we hope you enjoy building something you believe in and sharing it with the rest of the [i]Civ VII [/i]community! We can't wait to see what this amazing community will come up with next.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1295660/Sid_Meiers_Civilization_VII/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]
[/p]

tags.feature: As part of Update 1.2.2, Steam Workshop support is now live in Civilization VII! With the Civ VII Workshop, you can modify your journey through the Ages in Civilization VII with user-made leaders, civs, maps, Narrative Events, and more, then share them with the Civ community and rate your favorites to help boost their visibility!
We want to expand the functionality for Civ VII modding in the future, with the goal of making it even easier to build your own creations and share them with the world.
We're so excited to be adding the much-requested Steam Workshop to Civilization VII, and we hope you enjoy building something you believe in and sharing it with the rest of the Civ VII community!

notes.title: Sid Meier's Civilization VII Out Now!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=MGOdJMNN2b0;full][/previewyoutube]

Today's the day, [i]Civ [/i]fans – [i]Sid Meier's Civilization VII[/i] is available now!

To the entire [i]Civ [/i]community, thank you so much for joining us on this journey. We're honored and humbled to be starting this new chapter of [i]Civ [/i]history with you, and this is just the beginning of our years-long commitment to [i]Civilization VII[/i]. 

Thanks especially to everyone who has offered feedback and support in the days since Advanced Access began for Deluxe and Founders Edition owners. As we stated in our February 6 [url=https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/news/message-from-firaxis-games/]message to the [i]Civ [/i]community[/url], we're actively listening to all the feedback, and work is already underway on free updates to the game including a UI rework, the addition of community-requested features, and other quality-of-life updates. 

We're still determining what can be delivered when, so be on the lookout for a detailed roadmap in the future. We're committed to making [i]Civilization VII[/i] the best it can be, and your feedback is hugely helpful as we continue to make improvements.

[h2]Thank you for being a [i]Civ [/i]fan[/h2]

We can't wait for you to get into the game and start building an empire you believe in – but first, we'd like to share some heartfelt thanks to the entire [i]Civ[/i] community from some of the people who made [i]Civilization VII[/i] possible:

"Today is a monumental day for all of us at Firaxis, and we couldn't let it pass without saying a heartfelt thank you. When Sid Meier started this series over 30 years ago, his vision for [i]Civilization[/i] wasn't just about building a great game – it was about creating a canvas where players could shape the world and write their own history. That vision remains at the heart of everything we do, and it's what makes [i]Civilization VII[/i] a true collaboration with you, our dedicated fans. On behalf of everyone at Firaxis, thank you for your trust, excitement, and love for this series. Here's to the next chapter of [i]Civilization[/i]!" - [b]Heather Hazen, President of Firaxis[/b]

"The entire [i]Civilization[/i] team at Firaxis Games wants to send a big thank you out to our amazing community here on launch day. We are making some bold changes to elevate the [i]Civilization[/i] experience in innovative ways, and it has been so rewarding to see the trust our fans have in us when we try something new. We've been hard at work iterating on this new chapter for many years and are confident that we've hit on an amazing new formula you will truly enjoy. What's even better is that we can now begin our direct engagement with you, our fans, to take this new gameplay to even greater heights. Welcome to [i]Civ VII[/i]!" - [b]Ed Beach, Creative Director[/b]

"The journey that we're about to embark on has been years in the making. From the moment Ed Beach uttered the words 'history is built in layers' in late 2019, I knew that we were about to take ourselves and our fans into uncharted waters, and the journey has been filled with moments both challenging and rewarding. The moment everything starts to fall into place is an exciting one in game development, especially knowing that our fans who inspire us are about to encounter something that will challenge them in ways they are not expecting. It's with great excitement that we present to you our vision, and sincerely hope for many long nights taking just one more turn. We'll be there with you every step of the way, as our work is not done. We're just getting started." - [b]Dennis Shirk, Executive Producer[/b]

"Today's the day! We're thrilled to finally unveil the latest edition of our multi-decade, 4X-leading franchise, [i]Sid Meier's Civilization VII[/i], to the world. It's been years in the making, and we're beyond excited to share our new vision for [i]Civilization[/i]. This edition features the most expansive art content we've ever created, capturing thousands of years of human history from across the globe. We can't wait for our fans to dive in, spend countless hours exploring, and craft their own stories that span the history of humanity – and beyond!" - [b]Jason Johnson, Senior Art Director[/b]

[h2]How to share feedback[/h2]
If you get into the game and experience any issues, it’s hugely helpful for our team if you submit a ticket through our [url=https://support.civilization.com/hc/requests/new]feedback portal[/url] (select [i]Civ VII[/i] in dropdown). To see if an issue is already on our radar, you can check out [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fsupport.civilization.com%2Fhc%2Fen-us%2Fcommunity%2Ftopics%2F35818812180371-Civilization-VII]this page[/url] for known issues. Steam players are also encouraged to leave feedback and join the conversation in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1295660/discussions/][i]Civilization VII[/i] Steam Discussion forums[/url].

As part of our commitment to take in your feedback and keep you updated, we've soft-launched the official [url=https://discord.com/invite/civilizationofficial][i]Civilization [/i]Discord Server[/url] for English-speaking players (please mind our dust while we get things settled). This will be a new space for providing feedback, talking with other [i]Civ [/i]players, and getting updates directly from the dev team. We're still in beta, so join us while we continue to grow!

notes.title: This Week in Civ: Buganda, José Rizal, and Upcoming Livestreams
notes.content:
In case you missed it, here’s another roundup of [i]Civilization VII[/i] news from the past week:

Introducing Modern Age civ Buganda! [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/9beb29abc86455c5950b8adc3d5899af09c89c57.jpg[/img]

Watch live on February 8 at 5PM CET / 8 AM PT / 11AM ET on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/firaxisgames]Twitch[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/@civilization]YouTube[/url], or [url=https://www.facebook.com/civ]Facebook[/url]. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/7d19bae6d22fee179d98ae32f06ac67c199eb7af.jpg[/img]

The next few days are packed as we countdown to release! Keep an eye out for two more First Looks and two new civ guides, and don’t forget to tune in to our next developer livestream on January 30 covering multiplayer and post-launch. We’ll see you here next week, Civ fans!

notes.title: This Week in Civ: Ben Franklin, Harriet Tubman, and a Modern Age livestream!
notes.content:
In case you missed it, here’s another roundup of [i]Civilization VII[/i] news from the past week: 

[h2]Civ Reveal: America[/h2]
Our second Modern Age civ, revealed! America is all about expansion and industry, raking in Gold with its unique ability, Frontier Expansion. Check out the full [url=https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/civilizations/america/]game guide[/url] for all the details.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/114b17d023f517517b29be573fd577b14f574c25.jpg[/img]

[h2]First Looks: Harriet Tubman & Benjamin Franklin[/h2]

Two American East Coast heroes take the stage! Harriet Tubman is primed to outwit enemies with speed and espionage, with a powerful ability to ignore movement penalties from dense vegetation. Or, choose diplomat and innovator Ben Franklin - boosting science, diplomacy, and production while managing multiple Endeavors like a true polymath. Check out the game guides here for [url=https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/leaders/harriet-tubman/]Harriet Tubman[/url] and [url=https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/leaders/benjamin-franklin/]Ben Franklin[/url].

[previewyoutube=8Xe2DBSMT6A;full][/previewyoutube]

[previewyoutube=o7ZyxKitaO4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Modern Age Livestream[/h2]
That’s a wrap on the Modern Age! In the latest episode of Civ Streams, our devs took a deep dive into what’s coming to Modern, showing off industrialization, railroads, air combat, and more. Also, don’t miss seeing all the big reveals above in action. You can watch the full stream here: 

[previewyoutube=f7bqbpOrzd4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Mac & Linux Requirements[/h2]

Thanks for the patience of all our Mac and Linux players while we got the system requirements ready for you! We’ve updated our Steam page and added full details on those specs [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1295660/view/498308273994203442?l=english]here[/url]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/d150d54714dc78b114a22899f16e848bf48662c5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Coming up…[/h2]
Happy early holidays, Civ fans! Our devs will be taking a short break from content and recaps to rest up before the final push to February 11th. When we’re back, expect plenty more reveals and updates as we gear up for launch. If you haven’t preordered yet, don’t miss your chance to order the Deluxe or Founder’s Edition of [i]Civilization VII[/i] to start playing early on February 6th.

Here’s to your next great Golden Age in the New Year. We’ll see you soon!

notes.title: Civ VI Monthly Challenge: Civpocalypse
notes.content:
The new monthly challenge for Sid Meier's Civilization VI starts on December 10, and can be attempted on Prince or Emperor difficulty!

Each limited-time monthly challenge affords you an opportunity to test your skills as a specific leader in a unique scenario. The first time you successfully complete a challenge, you'll earn yourself a new in-game Hall of Fame Badge commemorating your impressive achievement!
To play the current monthly challenge, go to the main menu in-game and click on the "Challenge of the Month" image in the rotating marquee for your desired difficulty level. Note that if you don't own any of the DLC featured in the current challenge, you will be granted free trial access to it for use in the challenge so you won't miss out!

[h2]CURRENT CHALLENGE[/h2]
[b]CHALLENGE 14: Civpocalypse[/b]

[b]Duration: [/b]December 10 - January 15

In the latest Monthly Challenge, disaster strikes—again and again and again! As Tamar, ensure that Georgia can withstand whatever natural disasters and raging barbarian hordes come your way. As things get increasingly dire, you'll have to decide if you want to befriend other civs in a bid for shared survival or leave them to their own fate. With each passing turn, the cavalcade of catastrophes will only worsen; how long can you hold out?

You can pre-order Civilization VII now, with three editions to choose from: Standard Edition, Deluxe Edition, and the limited-time Founders Edition that's only available until February 28, 2025. For full details on what's included in each edition, visit the [url=https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/buy/]Civilization VII Buy page[/url] or the [url=https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/faq/]Civilization VII FAQs page[/url]!

Pre-ordering Civilization VII Standard Edition will grant you the Tecumseh and Shawnee Pack!* The Tecumseh and Shawnee Pack is included as part of the Deluxe Edition and Founders Edition. In addition, the Deluxe Edition and Founders Edition will grant early access for Civilization VII beginning on February 6, 2025.

You can also show the world your affinity for Civilization with the Sid Meier's Civilization® VII Collector's Edition, featuring a premium set of physical collectibles themed around Civilization VII! For more info, visit the [url=https://finalbossbundle.com/products/sid-meiers-civilization-vii-collectors-edition]Sid Meier's Civilization® VII Collector's Edition store page[/url]. [h2]Civilization VII Gameplay Trailer[/h2]

Alongside Civilization VII pre-orders going live, we revealed the first look at Civilization VII gameplay during Gamescom Opening Night Live with Geoff Keighley. Feast your eyes on the first-ever look at gameplay for this revolutionary new chapter in the Civilization series.

[previewyoutube=Tc3_EO6Bj2M;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Civilization VII Gameplay Showcase[/h2]

Following the Gamescom Opening Night Live presentation, we gave you an in-depth look at Civilization VII's finer details with the Civilization VII Gameplay Showcase on the [url=http://Twitch.tv/FiraxisGames]Firaxis Games Twitch channel[/url]. The showcase opens with a stirring live-action trailer starring Civilization VII's narrator: legendary actress Gwendoline Christie. 
The Civilization VII Gameplay Showcase has over 20 minutes of exclusive insights from the Firaxis development team, covering the vision for the game as well as its innovative new features. If you missed it, you can watch a VOD of the Gameplay Showcase above to soak up all the newly debuted game details!

[h2]Civilization VII Game Guide[/h2]

Knowledge is power, and the information in the Civilization VII Game Guide can help you prepare to build your perfect empire and determine which leaders and civilizations could best suit your preferred playstyle.

notes.title: Civ VI Monthly Challenge: Rotating Reduxes
notes.content:
[h3]A NOTE ABOUT THE 2K LAUNCHER AND [i]CIVILIZATION VI[/i] ON STEAM[/h3]

Alongside Challenge 10 going live on August 14, the new update also removes the 2K Launcher from [i]Sid Meier's Civilization VI[/i] on Steam. In addition, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1295660/Sid_Meiers_Civilization_VII/][i]Sid Meier's Civilization VII[/i][/url] will not use the 2K Launcher on PC.

---

The new monthly challenge for [i]Sid Meier's Civilization VI[/i] starts August 14! But this month, you're not getting just one event to take on: we're bringing back four fan favorites as week-long challenges with altered parameters! All four challenges can be played at Prince difficulty, or—if you reckon you're a certified Civ expert—the highest difficulty level of Deity.

The limited-time monthly challenges afford you an opportunity to test your skills as a specific leader in a unique scenario. The first time you successfully complete each challenge, you'll earn yourself a new in-game Hall of Fame Badge commemorating your impressive achievement. For PC players who already earned the Hall of Fame Badge for the original versions of these events, you can score a new Badge for your collection by completing the Redux version on Deity difficulty!

To play the current monthly challenge, go to the main menu in-game and click on the "Challenge of the Month" image in the rotating marquee. Note that if you don't own any of the DLC featured in the current challenge, you will be granted free trial access to it for use in the challenge so you won't miss out!

Read on for a breakdown of this month's four week-long challenges, and good luck out there! 


[h3]CHALLENGE 10 PART 1: SEVEN SEAS REDUX[/h3]

[b]Duration:[/b] August 14 - August 21

The continents have been consumed by oceans. Civilizations persist, scattered across the mountainous islands that remain, but for some it will prove nigh impossible to thrive in this unfamiliar environment. 

Playing as the Norwegian leader Harald Hardrada, you find yourself at an advantage. You've already explored most of the ocean, your Viking Longships are unrivaled in naval combat, and you have the unique ability to pillage your enemies' coastal tiles. During the Seven Seas challenge, played in Heroes & Legends mode, the victory condition you pursue is entirely up to you. That sea air sure smells like Domination, though!

For some general guidance related to this challenge, check out these [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=onb-hdjuNbU]Norway Overview[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EyLmqlvgdBI]Heroes & Legends Details[/url] video guides! 

[b]Redux Parameters[/b]
[list]
[*] Permanent Dark Age
[*] No Cavalry Barbarian Camps
[*] Naval Barbarian Camps spawn units twice as fast
[*] Hero Discovery Rate x2 for all AI leaders
[*] Water tiles deal 10 damage to all units
[/list]

[h3]CHALLENGE 10 PART 2: ROBOT REVOLUTION REDUX[/h3]

[b]Duration:[/b] August 21 - August 28

Do you have what it takes to ensure your civilization's survival for 100 turns in a frozen, post-nuclear future? This is your chance to prove it. Oh, and did we mention the robots?

Resources are sparse, disasters are intense, and Giant Death Robots are a constant threat. Your memory of life before the robot takeover is fading, but parts of the world are still known to you. As the Prime Minister of Canada, Wilfrid Laurier, will you scour the frozen wasteland for resources and remnants of the old world, or hunker down and hope to outlast your opponents? 

For some general guidance related to this challenge, check out this [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eg0PYsWK1dc]Canada Overview[/url] video guide!

[b]Redux Parameters[/b]
[list]
[*] All civilian units except builders and settlers are disabled
[*] Barbarian AI use of GDR is improved
[*] Civics, tech, and religion no longer give score towards victory condition
[*] World Congress is disabled
[/list]

[h3]CHALLENGE 10 PART 3: THREE STARS EACH REDUX[/h3]

[b]Duration:[/b] August 28 - September 4

The Babylonians were the first to record the cadence of the stars and planets in the sky. As Hammurabi, can you lead your people into space and secure a Science victory?

Technology and Civics trees are shuffled and hidden for this event, so Babylon's ability to unlock technological advancements via Eurekas is key. Adding to the unpredictability of this event, parameters including the map and other civilizations are randomized.

For some general guidance related to this challenge, check out these [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yo0aqclQjQw]Babylon Overview[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3NLoDMsqJkE]How to Generate Science[/url] video guides!

[b]Redux Parameters[/b]
[list]
[*] Babylon's Eureka ability applies to Civics as well as Science
[*] Science and Culture yields per pop are decreased by 99%
[/list]

[h3]CHALLENGE 10 PART 4: REACH FOR THE HEAVENS REDUX[/h3]

[b]Duration:[/b] September 4 - September 11

Originally designed by Civilization streamer Potato McWhiskey, this event challenges you to lead the Khmer Empire to a Culture victory. Build sprawling cities that celebrate your faith in the Prasat temples, and drive cultural hegemony through your population's growth.

The Khmer's wondrous Angkor Wat temple complex is a magnet for visitors in modern-day Cambodia. As King Jayavarman VII, can you attract enough tourists to achieve this goal?

For some general guidance related to this challenge, check out these [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=POvyttyA8EU]Khmer Overview[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MD9druFjSkg]How to Generate Culture[/url] video guides!

[b]Redux Parameters[/b]
[list]
[*] Military units beyond warrior and spearman are disabled
[*] Map type swapped to Arid
[*] No Bonus Resources (rice, wheat, etc.) on map
[/list]

CHALLENGE 9: LIVE YONGLE REACTION

As the leader of a great civilization you're no doubt accustomed to making difficult decisions. Scout or settler? Campus or commercial hub? Domination or diplomacy? And of course, the big one: Purple or Blue? For the latest challenge, the Civ VI community will decide whether Culture or Science victories reign supreme in the annals of history! 

During this Challenge of the Month, you can score points for Team Culture or Team Science by achieving either victory type as Yongle, with a collective point total for all players getting tallied up for the month. Will you be the hero of gifted artisans and sightseeing tourists everywhere by demonstrating the timeless value of Culture? Or would you rather champion the technological advancements and scholarly pursuits inherent to Science? The scores for Team Culture and Team Science during this challenge will be shared via the official @CivGame X feed, so be sure to check back and see how your chosen side is doing!

notes.title: CIV VI: AUGUST 2023 UPDATE INCLUDES NEW LEADER ABILITIES
notes.content:
We're excited to announce that a new update is now available for the Steam version of Civilization VI. In addition to addressing some reported issues, this update also improves the Leader Abilities of some of the Leaders introduced in [url=https://civilization.com/leader-pass/]Civilization VI: Leader Pass[/url].

Julius Caesar also benefits from an updated Leader Ability. If you haven't already, you can add him to your Civilization VI roster simply by linking your [url=https://accounts.2k.com/]2K Account[/url] to the account of the same platform that you use to play. [url=https://civilization.com/news/entries/add-julius-caesar-to-civilization-vi/]Here are instructions on how to create and link a 2K Account.[/url]


[h3]LEADER ABILITIES[/h3]

[b]Julius Caesar - Veni, vidi, vici[/b]
[b]New:[/b] +300 Gold whenever you conquer a city for the first time or when you earn Gold from a Barbarian Outpost. The Gold becomes 500 after researching Metal Casting and 700 after Steel (on Standard Speed). When targeting Barbarians, receive +5 Combat Strength and always earn normal XP.

[b]Old:[/b] Receive 200 Gold whenever you conquer a city for the first time or 100 Gold when you clear a Barbarian Outpost. These Gold amounts increase to 500 after you research Steel.

[b]Wu Zetian - Manual of Entrapment[/b]
[b]New:[/b] All Spies operate at 1 level higher. Whenever an offensive spy mission is successful, you also gain 100% of the Culture, Science, and Faith that the targeted city made that turn. Receive a free spy at Defensive Tactics and +1 Spy Capacity. You can purchase Spies with Faith.

[b]Old:[/b] All offensive Spies operate at 1 level higher. Whenever an offensive spy mission is successful, you also gain 50% of the Culture and Science that the targeted city earned that turn. Receive a free Spy (and extra Spy Capacity) after discovering Defensive Tactics.

[b]Harald Hadrada (Varangian) - Varangian Guard[/b]
[b]New:[/b] (Base game) 75% discount on levying units, and all units pay 2 less Gold maintenance. +1 Influence Point per turn from the Stave Church.

[b]Old: [/b](Base game) 75% discount on levying units, and all units pay 2 less Gold maintenance.

[b]New: [/b](Rise and Fall & Gathering Storm DLCs) All units pay 2 less Gold maintenance. 75% Discount on levying units, and levied units receive Culture, Faith, and Science from kills equal to 50% of the opponent's Combat Strength. +1 Influence Point per turn from the Stave Church.

[b]Old: [/b](Rise and Fall & Gathering Storm DLCs) 75% Discount on levying units, and levied units receive Culture, Faith, and Science from kills equal to 50% of the opponent's combat strength.

[b]Abraham Lincoln - Emancipation Proclamation[/b]
[b]New:[/b] Industrial Zones give +2 Amenities and +3 Loyalty per turn, but your Plantations give -2 Loyalty per turn. Receive a free Melee unit after constructing Industrial Zones and their buildings. The free unit does not require resources when created or to maintain and receives +5 Combat Strength.

[b]Old:[/b] (Base game) Industrial Zones give +2 Amenities. Receive a free Melee unit after constructing Industrial Zones and their buildings. The free unit does not require resources when created or to maintain and receives +5 Combat Strength.

[b]Old: [/b](Rise and Fall & Gathering Storm DLCs) Industrial Zones give +3 Loyalty per turn but your Plantations give -2 Loyalty. Receive a free Melee unit after constructing Industrial Zones and their buildings. The free unit does not require resources when created or to maintain and receives +5 Combat Strength.


[h3]AI UPDATES[/h3]
[list]
[*] Changed Kongolese leader Nzinga Mbande's preferred settlement placement; she now dislikes foreign settlement a great deal more.
[*] Fixed an issue that was preventing Barbarian attack forces from spawning properly on Immortal difficulty.
[/list]


[h3]ACHIEVEMENTS[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added Victory Achievements for Leaders introduced in Civilization VI: Leader Pass.
[*] Abraham Lincoln can no longer complete the "A Man A Plan A Canal Panama" Achievement that requires you to build the Panama Canal as Teddy Roosevelt.
[/list]


[h3]MISCELLANEOUS[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a reported issue that was preventing pillaged Dams from being repaired.
[*] Fixed a reported issue with Ottoman Empire leader Suleiman's (Muhtesem) secondary agenda not working properly.
[/list]

notes.title: Celebrate Julius Caesar's Birthday in Civilization VI!
notes.content:
On this day, July 12, in 100 BC, Julius Caesar was born in Suburra, Italy. To celebrate, we'd like to remind you that you can add the birthday boy to your roster of playable Civilization VI leaders by linking your [url=https://accounts.2k.com/en-US/]2K Account[/url] to the Steam Account that you use to play. You can find instructions on how to create and link a 2K Account below.

[previewyoutube=fHzG7NRubqQ;full][/previewyoutube]
Unsurprisingly, Caesar's military prowess makes him ideally suited to aggressive play in pursuit of Domination Victories, which are achieved by conquering the original Capital city of every other civilization. Waging war on a global scale is expensive, so making the most of Caesar's unique "Veni, Vidi, Vici" leader ability is key. With it, you receive 200 Gold whenever you conquer a city for the first time, or 100 Gold when you clear a Barbarian Outpost. Once you research Steel, these Gold amounts both increase to 500!

How will you choose to lead as Julius Caesar on his birthday? Perhaps you want to recreate history by playing on the True Start Location Earth Huge map? Or maybe you want to mix things up by interacting peacefully with some Barbarians in Barbarian Clans mode? Regardless of how you choose to celebrate as Caesar, we hope you have fun and emerge victorious!

[h3]Setting up and linking a new 2K Account[/h3]
Signing up for a 2K Account is easy! Simply go to 2K Account Signup and register. Once you’ve completed the sign-up, link your Steam account and boot up Civilization VI. Once in the game, log into your 2K Account.

You can also sign up for a 2K Account in-game. Simply click on the 2K Account button in the bottom right-hand corner of the main menu, then follow the instructions to register a new account.

[h3]Linking an existing 2K Account[/h3]
If you already have a 2K Account, all you need to do is boot up Civilization VI and log in to your 2K Account via the button in the bottom right-hand corner of the main menu. Once your account is linked, restart Civilization VI to add Caesar to your roster of leaders.

[i]*Offer available until November 24, 2024. Requires an Internet connection, a Steam copy of Civilization VI, and a 2K Account linked to the Steam account used to play the game. One per account. Void where prohibited. Terms apply.[/i]

notes.title: The Civilization VI Leader Pass continues - Meet the Rulers of England!
notes.content:
Sid Meier’s Civilization VI Leader Pass* concludes with the Rulers of England pack. Each Leader Pass release contains brand new leaders decked out with inventive abilities, each designed to tease out clever new playstyles and challenge veteran CIV players in surprising ways. You’ll also see a few familiar leaders, reinvented to represent them at a different stage on their journey through history. Forget the old ways and put your safe strategies to bed—the Civilization VI Leader Pass will forever change the way you rule.

[b]The Rulers of England includes:[/b][list]
[*] Elizabeth I
[*] Harald Hardrada (Varangian)
[*] Victoria (Age of Steam)
[/list]

[b]Elizabeth I[/b] constructed the foundations for the British Empire to come, but in her day, this was a desperate patchwork of privateers and spies amidst a world order dominated by other hostile powers. Trading’s a tough gig.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Drake's Legacy[/i]
[list]
[*] England's Trade Route Capacity is increased by 2 after acquiring your first Great Admiral. Trade Route to any city-state provide +3 Gold for every specialty district in the origin city. +100% Yields from Plundering Trade Routes.
[/list]

[b]Harald Hardrada (Varangian) [/b]takes on a new hue, reimagining the famed Norwegian at a different stage in his journey during a stint as a commander of the Byzantine Vangarian Guard.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Varangian Guard[/i]
[list]
[*] Base Game: 75% Discount on Levying units and all units pay 2 less maintenance.
[*] Rise and Fall + Gathering Storm: 75% Discount on Levying units and levied units receive Culture, Faith and Science From Kills equal to 50% of the opponent’s Combat Strength.
[/list]

[b]Victoria (Age of Steam) [/b]returns to CIV VI with a new focus. While her long reign marked great militaristic progress, which defined Victoria’s original CIV VI playstyle, she also ushered in great industrial change. Double down on industrial growth, get those cities hot and steamy.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Age of Steam[/i]
[list]
[*] +10% Production in Cities for every Industrial Zone building in that city. +2 Production to all Strategic Resources.      
[/list]

notes.title: The Civilization VI Leader Pass continues - Meet the Great Builders!
notes.content:
Sid Meier’s Civilization VI Leader Pass* continues with the Great Builders Pack. Each Leader Pass release contains brand new leaders decked out with inventive abilities, each designed to tease out clever new playstyles and challenge veteran CIV players in surprising ways. You’ll also see a few familiar leaders, reinvented to represent them at a different stage on their journey through history. Forget the old ways and put your safe strategies to bed—the Civilization VI Leader Pass will forever change the way you rule.

[b]The Great Builders includes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Sejong
[*] Ludwig II
[*] Theodora
[/list]

[previewyoutube=tzpuaaVU32M;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Sejong** [/b]is one of – if not the – most productive and famous leaders of Korea’s Joseon Dynasty, noted for invigorating Joseon’s infrastructure, science, and artistic life.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Hangul[/i]
[list]
[*] ]When you complete your first Technology from a new Era, receive double your Science per turn as Culture.     
[/list]


[b]Ludwig II [/b]was less interested in politics than in making the fairy tales of the region come to life. Known as “The Swan King” of the Catholic kingdom of Bavaria, it was under Ludwig that Bavaria lost its independence to Germany. Aspirational, but misguided.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Swan King[/i]
[list]
[*] Wonders, even if not finished, receive +2 Culture for every adjacent District. All Culture adjacencies provide Tourism after discovering Castles.      
[/list]    

[b]Theodora***[/b] was a former actress who rose to hold a powerful influence over her husband, the Emperor Justinian of the Byzantine Empire. She was instrumental in fortifying what would become Orthodox Christianity and in building the backbone of the Byzantines in an era of collapse elsewhere in the Empire.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Restorer of Icons[/i]
[list]
[*] Holy Sites provide Culture equal to their adjacency bonus. Farms provide a Faith adjacency to Hippodromes and Holy Sites.  
[/list]

 
[i]* Leader Pass content will be automatically delivered in-game as it is released.[/i]
[i]** Requires New Frontier Pass and Byzantium & Gaul Pack to play[/i]
[i]*** Requires Rise & Fall expansion to play[/i]

notes.title: The Civilization VI Leader Pass continues - Meet the Rulers of the Sahara!
notes.content:
Sid Meier’s Civilization VI Leader Pass continues with the Rulers of the Sahara pack*. Each Leader Pass release contains brand new leaders decked out with inventive abilities, all designed to tease out clever new playstyles and challenge veteran CIV players in surprising ways. You’ll also see a few familiar leaders, reinvented to represent them at a different stage on their journey through history.

[b]Rulers of the Sahara includes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Ramses II
[*] Cleopatra (Ptolemaic)
[*] Sundiata Keita
[/list]

[previewyoutube=jr5lEEr2hrE;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Ramses II’s [/b]reign is Egypt at the height of its power - his exploits are audacious, whether those be in carving monuments out of the living rock, or in carving the kingdoms of his enemies. Here is the pride and might of the pharaoh made flesh.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Abu Simbel[/i]
[list]
[*] Gain Culture equal to 15% of the construction cost when finishing Buildings and 30% when completing Wonders.
[/list]

[b]Cleopatra [/b]returns with a thematic focus on the Greek-speaking Ptolemaic dynasty, where Egypt formed the agricultural heart of the Mediterranean, and as such she brings a new leader ability that rewards food and culture pursuits over those of trade and gold.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Arrival of Hapi[/i]
[list]
[*] Resources along floodplains receive +1 food and +1 culture. +1 appeal on floodplains instead of standard -1.
[/list]

[b]Sundiata Keita**[/b] founded the Malian Empire from the ashes of Wagadou. He was a royal exile, who despite struggling with physical infirmity became an accomplished hunter, orator, and, eventually, king. Here is Mali in its pre-Islamic, pre-Mansa Musa state, a story of a struggle against nature, conniving enemies, and oneself. And over these, the Lion of Mali reigns triumphant.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Sogolon[/i]
[list]
[*] It costs 20% less gold to Recruit Great People and the Market gains 2 Great Writing slots. Great Works of Writing receive +4 Gold and +2 Production.    
[/list]

[i]*Base game and Leader Pass required to access Rulers of Sahara content.[/i][i][/i]

[i]**Requires Gathering Storm expansion to play.[/i]

notes.title: The Civilization VI Leader Pass continues - Meet the Rulers of China!!
notes.content:
Sid Meier’s Civilization VI Leader Pass continues with the Rulers of China pack. Each Leader Pass release contains brand new leaders decked out with inventive abilities, each designed to tease out clever new playstyles and challenge veteran CIV players in surprising ways. You’ll also see a few familiar leaders, reinvented to represent them at a different stage on their journey through history. Forget the old ways and put your safe strategies to bed—the Civilization VI Leader Pass will forever change the way you rule.

[b]Rulers of China includes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Yongle
[*] Wu Zeitan
[*] Qin Shi Huan
[/list]

[b]Yongle [/b]built the foundation for Ming’s international system and rebuilt its infrastructure. As emperor, he didn't overindulge in luxuries, but sought and received tributes from dozens of other countries.


[i]Unique Leader Ability: Lijia[/i]
[list]
[*] All Cities receive projects where they can convert 50% of their Production into Food, Faith, or 100% if it is Gold. (Base + Rise and Fall + Gathering Storm).
[*] Cities with 10 or more Population receive +2 Gold, +1 Science, and +1 Culture per turn for each Population in the city. (Gathering Storm + Rise and Fall)
[/list]

[b]Wu Zeitan[/b] was the only woman ever to sit on China's throne. She shifted the focus of power away from powerful families in favor of a more centralized bureaucracy and, by opening administrative examinations to all, moved Chinese politics towards a more meritocratic system.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Manual of Entrapment[/i]
[list]
[*] All offensive Spies operate at 1 level higher. Whenever an offensive spy mission is successful, you also gain 25% of the Culture and Science that the targeted city earned that turn. Receive a free spy after discovering Defensive Tactics.
[/list]

[b]Qin Shi Huang[/b] is remembered as a warlord who unified China, even going so far as to standardize weights and measures, make Chinese writing uniform, and issue a new Imperial currency.  He's also remembered for the creation of what we now know as the Terracotta Army, which was constructed to protect him in the afterlife.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Thirty-Six Stratagems[/i]
[list]
[*] Melee units receive the Converts Barbarian Action. This action transforms Barbarian units into your units.      
[/list]

notes.title: The Civilization VI Leader Pass begins now - Meet the Great Negotiators!
notes.content:
Sid Meier’s Civilization VI Leader Pass begins today, starting with The Great Negotiators. Each Leader Pass release contains brand new leaders decked out with inventive abilities, each designed to tease out clever new playstyles and challenge veteran CIV players in surprising ways. You’ll also see a few familiar leaders, reinvented to represent them at a different stage on their journey through history. Forget the old ways and put your safe strategies to bed—the Civilization VI Leader Pass will forever change the way you rule.

[b]The Great Negotiators includes:[/b] [list]
[*] Abraham Lincoln
[*] Nzinga Mbande
[*] Saladin [/list]
[previewyoutube=449t6cBctus;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Abraham Lincoln[/b] was President for only four years, but during that time he abolished slavery, successfully waged the Civil War, and catapulted the United States into the industrial age.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Emancipation Proclamation[/i]
[list]
[*] Gives Industrial Zones [u]extra loyalty[/u] and a [u]free unit[/u] when built, while reducing loyalty for each plantation.
[/list]

[b]Nzinga Mbande[/b], an important figure in Angolan history and in the early history of colonialism in Africa, struggled to establish a voice for herself (and a kingdom to rule), deftly bouncing between various kingdoms and playing the European powers off of each other all the while.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: Queen of Matambe and Ndongo[/i]
[list]
[*] Grants cities on the same continent as your capital extra yields but diminishes yields of cities on your home continent.
[/list]

[b]Saladin[/b] was the name given to him by his foes, but his allies knew him as Salah ad-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub, a Kurdish noble who rose to command the Arabic armies of the Faithful as the first sultan of Egypt and Syria. Saladin was given a military and religious education by his father Najm ad-Din Ayyub, former warden of the fortress at Tikrit.

[i]Unique Leader Ability: The Victorious[/i]
[list]
[*] Grants flanking and support bonuses to [u]all[/u] combat and religious units.
[/list]

These incoming leaders for existing civilizations are included as part of [url=https://civilization.com/anthology/]Civilization VI Anthology[/url] or available to purchase separately as part of the new [url=https://civilization.com/leader-pass/]Leader Pass[/url].* Each leader will arrive with a suite of surprising new or updated abilities alongside inventive new agendas that'll change the way you play when pursuing world domination.

[i]*[/i][i] Base game required to access Civilization VI: Leader Pass content. Some prior DLC required to play some content included in the Leader Pass.[/i]

notes.title: Add Julius Caesar to Civilization VI on November 21!
notes.content:
We're excited to announce that on November 21 you can add Julius Caesar to the game's roster!* To do so, simply link your [url=https://accounts.2k.com/]2K Account[/url] to the Steam account that you use to play. You can find instructions on how to create and link a 2K Account below.

Once you've linked your 2K Account, you'll need to restart Civilization VI and enable Julius Caesar. To do so, click Additional Content on the game's main menu followed by Mods, then scroll down through your list of additional content, click on "DLC: Julius Caesar," and click on the "Enable" button.

Where Civilization VI's default Roman leader Trajan has a penchant for civilizations with lots of territory and starts with a free building in all founded cities, Caesar is a conqueror. His dislike of Barbarians in-game is a nod to the successful campaign he waged against the tribes of Gaul during his time as a general circa 57 BC.

[previewyoutube=fHzG7NRubqQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]New Ability: Veni, vidi, vici[/h3]
[i]Receive 200 Gold whenever you conquer a city for the first time or 100 Gold when you clear a Barbarian Outpost. These Gold amounts both increase to 500 after you research Steel.[/i]

How will you choose to lead as Julius Caesar? Perhaps you want to recreate history by allying with Cleopatra? Maybe you relish the prospect of going toe-to-toe with a leader like the German king Frederick Barbarossa, who became Rome's Holy Emperor a millennium and change after Caesar ruled there? Regardless of how you lead, we hope you enjoy playing as and against one of history's greatest military commanders.


[h3]Setting up and linking a new 2K Account[/h3]
Signing up for a 2K Account is easy! Simply go to [url=https://accounts.2k.com/signup]2K Account Signup[/url] and register. Once you’ve completed the sign-up, link your Steam account and boot up Civilization VI. Once in the game, log into your 2K Account.

You can also sign up for a 2K Account in-game. Simply click on the 2K Account button in the bottom right-hand corner of the main menu and then follow the instructions to register a new account.


[h3]Linking an existing 2K Account[/h3]
If you already have a 2K Account, all you need to do is boot up Civilization VI and then log in to your 2K Account via the button in the bottom right-hand corner of the main menu. Once your account is linked, restart Civilization VI to add Caesar to your roster of leaders.

 

[i]*Requires an Internet connection, a Steam copy of Civilization VI, and a 2K Account linked to the Steam account used to play the game. One per account. Void where prohibited. Terms apply.[/i]

notes.title: Civ 6's April patch brings welcome balance to a complex 4X game
notes.content:
Last week, Firaxis released its biggest Civilization 6 balance patch to date. The April 2021 update includes significant changes to just over half the existing Civ 6 civilisations and adds new combat units. It also introduces new cultural domination incentives, huge Earth and True Start Location maps and even a feature allowing scouts to pet their dogs. For the most part, fans have welcomed these changes, though some fussy Redditors had hoped for more.

The patch, billed as the final free update of the New Frontier season pass, addresses many of the most common complaints. Combining player feedback and data-driven analysis, Firaxis has sought to give the 4X game a face lift.

The result shows what it means to really end on a high note. The patch injects new life into several formerly weak civilisations while nerfing others many considered overpowered. The new units offer more options for early- and mid-game combat - critical stages of the game. Overall, the update refreshes aspects of Civ 6 that would otherwise have become stale in the wake of the New Frontier Pass.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Civilization 6's big April balance patch has dropped - here's what it changes
notes.content:
The massive Civilization 6 April balance patch is finally here, and it's a whopper. The update introduces three new military units, four new map types, and makes a host of other tweaks and changes. On top of that, 27 Civ 6 civs (and in some cases, leaders) have been given a balance pass to try and refresh the game's meta as the New Frontier Pass comes to the close.

And that's not all: 44 units from across the game's 10+ unit types have received tweaks to stats such as costs, combat strength and in certain cases, what techs are used to unlock them. The inclusion of the Trebuchet, Line Infantry and Men-at-arms has also caused a slight shift in military progression, and many civilisation's unique units have changed what vanilla unit they're replacing. For example, the British's Redcoat infantry and France's Garde Impériale both now replace the new Line Infantry.

The thrust of the update seems to be aimed at legacy content stretching back to launch and the earlier expansion, although plenty of new elements from the New Frontier Pass have also had a touch-up in the April patch.

Read the rest of the story...
